# dsh-academic-skills

> **Scope:** this port serves **five** ARS skills — `academic-paper-reviewer`,
> `deep-research`, `a

cademic-paper`, `sr-screener` and `academic-pipeline` — and
> only the reviewer has tools, review st

ate and a GUI panel. The other four are
> prompt-only: `deep-research` is a research pipeline, `acad

emic-paper` a writing
> pipeline, `sr-screener` a screening pipeline whose usefulness depends on run

ning
> its own bundled Python scripts on your host (`Python 3.9+`; this plugin ships
> those scripts

and never runs them), and `academic-pipeline` an orchestrator that
> dispatches the other three, wh

ose integrity stages need the upstream repository and
> a Python 3 environment this port deliberatel

y does not ship (see
> the honest edge). Reviewer input is
> `.md` / `.tex` / `.txt` only: there is

no PDF parsing and no OCR.
> The plugin's own tools and commands never rewrite your manuscript (see

> Write policy A). All five served skills carry
> the same rule as an *instruction* prepended to the

body — the same 684 bytes in
> every skill, whether or not it writes. It is not enforcement.

An **unofficial DSH port** of the Academic Research Skills (ARS) skills
`academic-paper-reviewer`, `

deep-research`, `academic-paper`, `sr-screener` and
`academic-pipeline` for DeepSeek Harness. It is

not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by the upstream
author or project.

The plugin serves all five vendored upstream skills through one DSH skill
provider. Only the reviewe

5-seat peer-review panel needs (an immutable per

SHA-256 pinning, and the two human checkpoints the upstream protocol

## What this plugin provides
### What this port does not ship — the port notice

A served skill is upstream text, and upstream text sometimes tells the agent to open a
file that liv

es in a *different* ARS skill or in the upstream repository itself. This
port cannot ship those, so

it says so. When a served skill's **own** instructions name
a file this package does not contain, th

e provider appends a delimited block to the
served body — runtime text only, the vendored files them

selves are never edited — and
carries the full list in `metadata.unavailableReferences` /
`metadata.

unavailableReferenceCount`. The model is told, in the notice, not to
fabricate the missing content.

**One of the five skills earns a notice today: `academic-pipeline`, 853 bytes naming
four targets.**

Its tree names `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`, two `docs/design/` specs and
the `scripts/adapters/` director

### Why are there five tools?

One tool per state transition, so the model can see exactly what it is allowed
to do next and branch
on a machine-readable error code instead of prose:
| Tool | Transition it owns |

| `academic_review_create` | pins the manuscript, opens the review and the panel |
| `academic_revie

w_confirm` | human checkpoint 1 only — the single path out of `created` |
| `academic_review_submit`

| one immutable seat card per call |
| `academic_review_report` | synthesis, then the approval-gate

d close |
| `academic_review_status` | read-only summary, including the pending checkpoint |

They are adapters: every validation, schema check and atomic write lives in
`src/state.ts`, which th

e slash commands drive through the same store.
Splitting them keeps the dangerous operation (`confir

m`) separate from the
routine ones, and leaves no single "do everything" call that could skip a gate

`) separate from the
routine ones, and leaves no single "do everything" call that could skip a gate.
### Why are there two human checkpoints?

Both come from the upstream protocol's iron rules and are enforced in state,
never by prompt text:

1. **After the field analysis, before any seat is dispatched**
(`field_analysis_attachment` → `panel

_confirmation`). The field analyst
proposes the discipline, paradigm, methodology, tier and maturity

plus one
reviewer configuration card per peer seat. Panel composition is the user's
call, so `acade

mic_review_confirm(action="confirm")` must record their
approval; `academic_review_submit` refuses w

ith `panel_not_confirmed`
until then, and nothing self-confirms.
2. **Before the editorial decision

closes the review** (`report_approval`).
Synthesis writes a draft letter and roadmap; closing requir

es
`academic_review_report(approve=true)`, and if the Devil's Advocate raised a
CRITICAL finding, ev

ery such finding must carry an explicit adjudication
(`da_adjudication_required` otherwise). The plu

gin never approves its own
output and a DA-CRITICAL issue cannot be silently bypassed.
